title: Formalisation of toric varieties in Lean 4

source.citation: Cox, Little, Schenck, Toric Varieties, AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 124, 2011
source.scope: Ch. 1 (affine toric varieties: cones, affine monoids, toric ideals), plus Hopf-algebra / diagonalisable group background from Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017)
source.evidence: README: "The definitions, theorems and proofs in this repository are taken from Toric varieties by Cox, Little and Schenck"; but blueprint: "We do not follow the proof from \cite{Cox_2011}", "See Lemma 12.4 in \cite{Milne_2017}", many "Classic. See \cite{Oda_1988} maybe". Page estimate: CLS Ch. 1 ~45 pp.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Group-like elements: An element $a$ of a coalgebra $A$ is \emph{group-like} if $\eta(a) = 1$ and $\Delta(a) = a \otimes a$, where $\eta$ is the counit and $\Delta$ is the comultiplication map. We write $\mathrm{GrpLike} A$ for the set of group-like elements of
edge_sample.target_text: proposition Galois connection between group algebra and group-like elements: Let $R$ be a domain, $G$ a commutative group and $A$ a $R$-bialgebra. Then bialgebra homs $R[G] \to A$ are in bijection with group homs $G \to \mathrm{GrpLike} A$.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Diagonalizable bialgebras: A bialgebra is called diagonalizable if it is isomorphic to a group algebra.
edge_sample.target_text: corollary : A bialgebra over a domain is diagonalizable if and only if it is spanned by its group-like elements.

edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Let $\tau$ be a face of a polyhedral cone $\sigma$. If $v, w \in \sigma$ and $v + w \in \tau$, then $v, w \in \tau$.

edge_sample.source_text: proposition Embedding an affine monoid inside a lattice: If $M$ is an affine monoid, then $M$ can be embedded inside ${\mathbb Z}^n$ for some $n$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : $i : R[M] \hookrightarrow R[{\mathbb Z} M]$ injects into an integral domain so is an integral domain. It's finitely generated by $\chi^{a_i}$ where $\mathcal A = \{a_1, \dotsc, a_s\}$ is a finite generating set for $M$.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Spec as a functor on algebras: Spec is a contravariant functor from the category of $R$-algebras to the category of schemes over $\mathrm{Spec}_R$.
edge_sample.target_text: proposition Spec as a functor on algebras is fully faithful: Spec is a fully faithful contravariant functor from the category of $R$-algebras to the category of schemes over $\mathrm{Spec}_R$, preserving all limits.

edge_sample.source_text: proposition : Let the base be $S=\mathrm{Spec} k$ for a field $k$, then $Y_{\mathcal A}$ is a toric variety.
proposition Bialgebras are comonoid objects in the category of algebras: The category of $R$-bialgebras is equivalent to comonoid objects in the category of $R$-algebras.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Relative interior: The {\bf relative interior}, aka {\bf intrinsic interior}, of a cone $\sigma$ is the interior of $\sigma$ as a subset of its span.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma Minimal face of a cone: If $\sigma$ is a cone, then $W := \sigma \cap (-\sigma)$ is a subspace. Furthermore, $W = H_m \cap \sigma$ whenever $m \in \mathrm{Relint}(\sigma^\vee)$.
